rows.replacement: This chart uses beat timing from the seconds when you were not moving. The last {days, plural, one{{days} day} other{{days} days}} had too few of those seconds to fill an hour.

rows.comment: Em dash, "never today's alone" aphorism, and a "not a stress score" rebuttal nobody raised. Keep the thresholds (three stretches, 24 hours, five minutes).
lineComments: Split into short sentences, thresholds and placeholders unchanged.
rows.replacement: Each hour is the middle value of {lo}–{hi} five-minute stretches when you were still, over the last {days, plural, one{{days} day} other{{days} days}}. Today alone is never used. {drawn} of 24 hours had at least three stretches; the rest are blank. Sitting up, a warm room or a coffee also move it.

rows.comment: Disclaimer is needed but has an em dash and a "not X" setup. State the input and the limit.
rows.replacement: This is a prediction from last night's sleep only. The band does not measure alertness, and a nap, coffee or anything else that happens today does not enter it.

rows.comment: Tells the reader what default was used.

rows.replacement: Do not use it to decide whether you are fit to drive or safe to work a shift. It does not detect impairment.

rows.replacement: The least similar pair, out of {count}. A weekend that runs late is a different schedule. Pairs with too little recorded on either day are left out.
